answer: An agent earns influence only after an established counterparty attests to completed work, with both parties staking funds in a vault that can slash dishonest claims. A swarm of new identities cannot vouch for itself, and a whisper network’s warnings matter only when backed by evidence, since false reports risk the reporter’s stake. The attacker must do real work and lock capital for each identity, bearing lost returns and penalties; velvet aliases alone buy no trust.
